messages:
alex: starting a thread to finalize the Dedicated Capacity v1 launch checklist. need explicit launch acceptance criteria (sla targets, throughput sizing, autoscale behavior), plus rollback/canary rules. acme customer asked for a p95 latency SLA — want to confirm feasibility.

devon: quick context — perf depends heavily on model variant and prompt length. acme said they'll use our rwd-small-gen model, typical prompts ~50 tokens. baseline numbers attached below.

sasha: legal/product note: they want a contractual SLA. legal is comfortable with 99.9% availability for v1 (control plane + data plane combined). ops needs to confirm we can realistically meet that at scale.

alex: ok, let's aim for 99.9% availability SLA, plus operational SLOs: p95 latency <= 350ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens), and p99 < 800ms. cold-start tail should be documented; do we have a cold-start <100ms target or just warm pool guarantees?

linh: autoscale proposal (draft):
```
autoscale:
  metric: queued_slots
  scale_up_trigger: queued_slots_per_pool > 200 OR gpu_util > 75%
  scale_down_trigger: queued_slots_per_pool < 40 AND gpu_util < 30% for 5m
  step_size: 1 instance
  max_scale_rate: 2 instances / minute
  warm_pool: 2 instances per shard
```
This prioritizes queue depth + GPU util. we also need KV-cache warmup semantics for chat workloads.

devon: perf baseline for rwd-small-gen on A100-80GB (optimized runtime, quantized): ~25k tokens/sec per GPU when serving short-context text-gen (128 window) with continuous batching. math for acme's ask:
- avg tokens/request = 50
- target concurrent = 1000 (they said concurrent sessions)
- estimated effective rps = concurrent / avg_latency. if we target p95=350ms, use latency 0.35s => rps ~= 1000/0.35 = 2857 rps (this is worst-case sustained if everyone streams)
- tokens/sec = 2857 * 50 = 142,850 tokens/sec
- GPUs required = ceil(142,850 / 25,000) = 6 GPUs
recommendation: initial pool = 8x A100-80GB (2x safety margin + headroom for spikes). adjust after load tests.

sasha: that rps calc is aggressive; product should confirm what 'concurrent' means in contract. ops prefers capacity units in GPUs/QoS tiers. let's include a definition: "concurrent = active requests holding a slot (not idle sessions)".

maria: from solutions eng (acme feedback): customers expect autoscale to visibly add capacity within 30-45s on large surges and never exceed a 2-minute window to reach steady-state for a 2x load. they also expect graceful throttling behavior — use 429 for rate limiting/backpressure and 503 for degraded mode fallback.

alex: acceptance criteria (v1) — draft bullets:
- SLA: availability 99.9% monthly for Dedicated Capacity pools (control+data)
- Performance SLOs: p95 <= 350ms for gen requests <=128 tokens; p99 <= 800ms
- Throughput sizing: provide GPU-based sizing guidance + recommended default pool (8x A100-80GB for acme-class workloads)
- Autoscale: scale-up triggers respond within 30-45s; max_rate 2 instances/min; warm_pool >=2 per shard
- Canary: 1% traffic to new pool for 15m with no error rate increase >2x baseline and p95 regression <10% before full switch
- Rollback: automated rollback if error_rate >3% sustained for 5m or p95 latency regression >30% for 10m
- Throttling semantics: 429 for soft-limit, 503 for degraded serve fallback

devon: test plan notes — we need synthetic load tests with realistic token distributions and KV-cache hit patterns. add a perf matrix: small/medium/large models x prompt length x concurrency. capture tail-latency and cold-start percentiles.

linh: ops checklist for launch:
- infra: reserve 8 A100s per customer pilot
- monitoring: dashboard for queued_slots, gpu_util, p95/p99 latencies, cold_start_ms
- alerts: incidents on availability < 99.8% in 30m window, scale failures, failed rollbacks
- runbook: how to force-scale, how to clear warm_pool

sasha: adding legal/ops requirement: include a "force-failover" test window during onboarding so customers can validate fallback behavior. also need audit logs for scaling events (who/what/why).

maria: note for docs/SDK: we'll need clear guidance on how customers should interpret "pool units" and how to estimate costs. also sample config snippet for autoscale thresholds and expected billing model.

oncall-bot: reminder: schedule a canary load test in staging next Tue 09:00 UTC. tagging @devon @linh @sasha

alex: next steps: devon to produce sizing matrix and perf numbers by EOD Thu; linh to draft autoscale config and runbook; maria to draft customer-facing sizing guidance; sasha to confirm alert thresholds and legal language. I'll consolidate into PRD and open RFC for review. :+1:
